Package com.cdarobotics.cdalib.subsystems

Class ThreadedIMU

java.lang.Object
com.cdarobotics.cdalib.subsystems.Subsystem
com.cdarobotics.cdalib.subsystems.ThreadedIMU
public class ThreadedIMU extends Subsystem
A Subsystem that reads the IMU on its own background thread so the main loop never blocks on it.

The universal IMU is an I2C device, and I2C is not covered by Lynx bulk caching — so a normal getRobotYawPitchRollAngles() in the loop costs a full blocking transaction (several milliseconds) every cycle. This subsystem instead spins a reader thread that polls the IMU continuously and publishes each reading to a cached snapshot; the getters return that snapshot in constant time, removing IMU latency from every loop.

Register it with registerSubsystem(...) in your preload() — ModularOpMode then starts the reader thread on start() and stops it on OpMode end. The IMU must already be initialized (via imu.initialize(...) with your hub orientation) before this subsystem is registered; like IMUDevice it does not initialize the IMU itself.

All hardware access to the IMU (the periodic read and resetYaw()) is serialized on an internal lock, so it is safe to call resetYaw() from the loop thread while the reader thread is running. Getters return 0 until the first reading lands.

    • resetYaw

      public void resetYaw()

    • getImu

      public com.qualcomm.robotcore.hardware.IMU getImu()
      Returns:
      the wrapped SDK IMU. Direct calls from the loop thread race with the reader thread; synchronize on nothing exposed here — prefer the getters and resetYaw().
